$comment: Latency cache for the source-leak gate's repository-visibility probe: names the probe may clear WITHOUT an API call. It is not an authority for 'private' — a name absent from this list, or present but older than ttlDays, is resolved live against the API, so the list may be short and still be correct. Each entry records the day the name was last confirmed public against the API; a cache entry that cannot go stale would be a permanent fail-open, because a repository turned private later would keep clearing forever. It is deliberately NOT a mirror of every public repository in the organization: only repositories that are public by construction (the OSS product surfaces every caller cites constantly) belong here, and an entry is REMOVED rather than a new one accumulated when that stops being true. Metadata is validated fail-closed, because a cache that keeps vouching is the failure that matters: `ttlDays` must be an INTEGER in 1..7 (anything else — a huge TTL, 0, a fraction, a string — is the freshness rule switched off, so the WHOLE cache is ignored with one warning line and every name resolves live; omitting it takes the shipped 7-day default), and each `verifiedAt` must be a canonical YYYY-MM-DD day that round-trips as a real calendar date (2026-02-30 does not — Date silently normalises it to March 2nd) and is not in the future (UTC); an entry failing either check is treated as stale and resolved live, never as verified. Regenerate with `--verify-cache`; the weekly refresh workflow does it and opens a pull request on drift.
